meta.abstract:
Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) is an Orlando, Florida-based technology commercialization platform that identifies, licenses, and operates companies built around breakthrough technologies acquired from multinational corporations. Founded in 2015 by co-founder and Executive Chairman Mike Otworth — whose company-creation methodology traces directly to XL TechGroup, the firm that generated $4.5 billion of public-market value through six IPOs in the 1990s — Innventure executes a disciplined 'Found, Fund, Operate' model targeting dormant corporate intellectual property using its proprietary MATCH scoring framework (Market, Advantage, Timeline, Capital, High Value).

The platform's most prominent proof of concept is PureCycle Technologies (NASDAQ: PCT), which Innventure built from a polypropylene-recycling technology licensed from Procter & Gamble in 2015 and took to a billion-dollar Nasdaq listing in March 2021. With PureCycle now an independent public company, Innventure's current portfolio comprises three active operating companies: Accelsius, a two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling company serving the AI data-center market that completed a Series B at a $665 million post-money valuation in December 2025 with strategic investors Johnson Controls and Legrand; AeroFlexx, a sustainable flexible liquid-packaging company founded on P&G's Air Assist technology that has secured a global commercial partnership with Aveda (Estée Lauder); and Refinity, a plastic-waste-to-chemical-intermediates venture launched in December 2024 in collaboration with The Dow Chemical Company.

Innventure itself went public on October 3, 2024, completing a SPAC business combination with Learn CW Investment Corp. Full-year 2024 revenue totaled $1.2 million as operating companies remained in early commercialization; a $233 million goodwill impairment charge in Q1 2025 triggered a going-concern qualification and required a $40 million registered direct offering in January 2026. Accelsius's $1 billion-plus sales pipeline, its DarkNX 300-megawatt AI campus deployment in Ontario, Canada, and analyst consensus price targets of $14.50 against a May 2026 share price of approximately $6.38 frame a high-convexity thesis centered on whether management can execute the transition from technology incubation to scaled revenue generation.

chapters.title: The Spinout Factory: Innventure's Thesis and Its Moment of Reckoning
chapters.body:
On the morning of October 3, 2024, Bill Haskell stood at the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square to ring the opening bell as Innventure, Inc. began trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker INV. The ceremony marked the completion of a business combination with [Learn CW Investment Corp](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0002001557&type=10-K), a SPAC vehicle, and it carried a symbolic charge that extended well beyond a standard small-cap listing. For the first time, a technology-commercialization platform — a company whose entire value proposition rests on the thesis that multinational corporations are sitting atop dormant billion-dollar businesses — had submitted itself to the scrutiny of public markets.

## The Thesis: Unlocking Dormant IP

The proposition is at once elegant and audacious. Innventure, co-founded in 2015 by Mike Otworth and shaped by the methodology Haskell developed during his decade at XL TechGroup, operates as a permanent owner-operator of companies built around technologies licensed or acquired from large industrial and consumer-goods corporations. Its MATCH framework — evaluating opportunities across Market, Advantage, Timeline, Capital, and High Value dimensions — and its proprietary DownSelect® due-diligence process are designed to identify the roughly 70 percent of breakthrough corporate innovations that, by Innventure's own research, never reach the market. The proof of concept arrived early: Innventure licensed Procter & Gamble's proprietary polypropylene-recycling chemistry in 2015, founded PureCycle Technologies around it, and took the company to a Nasdaq SPAC IPO in March 2021 at a valuation exceeding $1 billion. PureCycle established the template. At the May 2026 snapshot date, three live experiments — Accelsius, AeroFlexx, and Refinity — are running simultaneously against that template.

## Ambition Meets the Balance Sheet

The distance between platform ambition and financial reality, however, is considerable. Full-year 2025 net revenue reached approximately [$2.06 million](https://ir.innventure.com/financial-information/sec-filings) — a 69 percent increase over 2024's $1.22 million, but a figure that remains pre-scale by any conventional measure. The consolidated net loss for FY2025 was approximately ~~$171 million~~ ==$475.4 million ($293.3 million attributable to Innventure stockholders)==, and the FY2024 10-K carried a going-concern qualification from auditors. The proximate cause was ~~a $233.2 million goodwill impairment charge in Q1 2025, which drove a quarterly net loss of $253.7 million and reduced consolidated cash to approximately $1.4 million~~ ==$346.6 million in FY2025 goodwill impairments — $233.2 million of which was recognized in Q1 2025, driving a $253.7 million quarterly net loss and reducing consolidated cash to approximately $1.4 million at the March 31, 2025 trough== before Innventure completed a $40 million registered direct offering in January 2026 to ~~restore operating runway~~ ==improve near-term liquidity, though going-concern and capital-access risk were not extinguished==. At the May 2026 snapshot date, the company carried a market capitalization of approximately $536 million — a figure almost entirely underpinned by investor confidence in Accelsius's commercial trajectory rather than any current earnings power.

| Metric | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Net revenue | $1.22M | ~$2.06M |
| Net loss | $98.8M | ~~$171M~~ ==~$475.4M (total); ~$293.3M attributable== |
| Adj. EBITDA | -$27.9M | ~~n/a~~ ==-$78.8M== |
| ~~Cash (period-end)~~ ==Cash== | $11.1M | ~$1.4M (Q1 2025 trough) |

## The Three Live Experiments

**Accelsius** is Innventure's most commercially advanced and most capital-intensive position. Founded in 2022 ==around Nokia-origin patent and technology agreements==, it commercializes two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling for AI data centers through its NeuCool® product family, with demonstrated capability to dissipate 4,500 watts per socket — performance that neither air cooling nor single-phase liquid cooling can match at the thermal design powers demanded by the latest AI accelerator chips. Accelsius completed a $24 million Series A and, in December 2025, a fully funded Series B with strategic investors Johnson Controls and Legrand at a post-money valuation of [$665 million](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/04/3249263/0/en/Innventure-Operating-Companies-Advance-to-Independent-Capital-Formation-as-Platform-Momentum-Accelerates.html), with management guiding toward cash-flow positivity by year-end 2026. Its active sales pipeline exceeds $1 billion.

**AeroFlexx**, founded in 2018 around P&G's Air Assist flexible-packaging technology, produces a self-standing film pouch requiring up to 85 percent less virgin plastic than conventional rigid bottles. It holds Association of Plastic Recyclers Critical Guidance recognition for recyclability, carries a global commercial partnership with Aveda (Estée Lauder Companies) as its first prestige beauty customer, and has established a European manufacturing collaboration with Chemipack in Poland. It addresses a stated $400 billion global addressable market across personal care, household, and industrial fluid categories.

**Refinity**, the newest and most nascent of the three, was founded in December 2024 ~~in partnership with The Dow Chemical Company~~ ==around VTT-origin licensed technology, with The Dow Chemical Company as collaboration, channel, and commercialization partner,== to convert mixed plastic waste streams into drop-in petrochemical feedstocks. Pilot-scale validation has been completed; commercial demonstration plant financing and construction remain multi-year milestones.

## The Question That Frames Everything

PureCycle Technologies answered the foundational question about Innventure's model: it is possible, given the right technology, the right market moment, and the right execution, to extract a billion-dollar business from dormant corporate intellectual property. The question the next four years will answer is harder — and it is the question that gives this dossier its shape. Can the same model work on three companies simultaneously, across three different end-markets, inside a single public holding company operating with a balance sheet that nearly ran dry eighteen months into its public existence?

chapters.title: Found, Fund, Operate: From XL TechGroup's $4.5 Billion Legacy to the Innventure Platform
chapters.body:
## The XL TechGroup Blueprint

Long before Innventure, Inc. rang the opening bell on the Nasdaq Global Market in October 2024, the company's core intellectual architecture had already been tested — and validated — across nearly two decades of company creation at XL TechGroup. Founded in 1993, XL TechGroup operated from a premise that was radical by the standards of the era: that the most underexploited asset class in the American economy was the proprietary science sitting dormant inside large corporations, and that a specialist operator with the right sourcing discipline, team-assembly protocols, and milestone-gated capital framework could extract value that incumbent R&D bureaucracies demonstrably could not.

The results were concrete. By the time the platform wound down its most active phase, XL TechGroup had generated approximately $4.5 billion of public-market value through six IPOs across U.S. and London Stock Exchange markets. That track record was not the product of financial engineering. It was the product of a repeatable operating system: find a technology with verified scientific merit languishing inside a major corporation, license or acquire it on defensible terms, assemble a purpose-built management team around the specific commercial challenge, and deploy capital in tranches calibrated to technical and commercial milestones rather than calendar schedules.

Bill Haskell was inside that architecture from the beginning. A graduate of Iowa State University with a B.S. in Engineering and post-graduate work in applied mathematics, Haskell spent his early career as an applied mathematician working on space-borne imaging platforms — a domain that trained him in the intersection of rigorous quantitative modeling and long-cycle hardware development. He co-founded XL Vision in 1993, then co-founded XL TechGroup itself, where he served as president through 2011. In that role he executed IPO processes, sat on the boards of more than a dozen companies, and served as CEO of a London Stock Exchange-listed company — accumulating the precise credentials that Innventure would later require of its public-company leadership.

## Otworth's Trajectory: An Iterative Thesis

Mike Otworth arrived at the same fundamental thesis by a different path. His career began on Capitol Hill, where he worked as a legislative aide and committee staff member — an apprenticeship in the mechanics of institutional power, regulatory influence, and the politics of industrial policy that would prove relevant when navigating corporate licensing negotiations with multinational R&D organizations. He joined XL TechGroup in 1996 and spent four years inside the platform's company-creation machinery before departing at the turn of the century.

The period between XL TechGroup and Innventure was not dormant. From 2008 to 2015, Otworth served as president and founding partner of Green Ocean Innovation, a technology-sourcing and innovation-strategy consultancy whose primary client relationship was with Lilly and its subsequent animal-health spinout, Elanco. That engagement sharpened the sourcing half of the thesis: Otworth was specifically engaged to identify and unlock technologies that Lilly's internal commercialization infrastructure was failing to advance. By 2015, the consultancy model had run its logical course. Otworth concluded that the most effective expression of the underlying insight — that corporate R&D assets are systematically undercommercialized — was not advisory but operational: a permanent platform that would source, capitalize, and operate companies, retaining ownership through the commercialization inflection rather than handing off after the licensing transaction.

That platform was Innventure.

## PureCycle: The Proof-of-Concept

The first test of Innventure's methodology was unambiguous in its ambition. In 2015, the same year the platform was established, Otworth licensed Procter & Gamble's proprietary polypropylene-recycling process from P&G Research Fellow Dr. John Layman and founded PureCycle Technologies around it. The technology addressed a material science problem that the plastics recycling industry had failed to solve for decades: the ability to purify post-consumer polypropylene — the second most widely used plastic in the world — back to near-virgin resin specifications, removing color, odor, and contaminants in a single-solvent process that was both scalable and economically competitive with virgin resin production.

Otworth served as PureCycle's founding chief executive from 2015 through 2022, shepherding the company from a laboratory science license through pilot-plant construction, first-plant financing, and the company-building sequence that Innventure had codified at XL TechGroup: assemble a domain-specific management team, gate capital deployment to technical milestones, and drive toward a public-market liquidity event that would establish value for both the operating company and the parent platform.

In March 2021, PureCycle Technologies completed a SPAC IPO on the Nasdaq at a valuation exceeding $1 billion, transitioning to independent public status as PCT. The outcome established the proof of concept in the most legible terms available to capital markets: a technology sourced from a corporate laboratory, founded into a standalone company by Innventure's methodology, had achieved the billion-dollar enterprise value target that Otworth had set as the platform's benchmark.

## AeroFlexx and Accelsius: Platform Expansion

Innventure did not wait for PureCycle to reach its commercial inflection before deploying the methodology again. In 2018, three years after founding PureCycle and while Otworth was still serving as its CEO, the platform founded AeroFlexx around P&G's Air Assist flexible-packaging technology — work developed by P&G Research Fellow Ken McGuire. The technology uses compressed air to stiffen the edges of a flexible film pouch, producing a self-standing package that requires up to 85 percent less virgin plastic than conventional rigid bottles while remaining recyclable in standard plastic-bottle collection streams. AeroFlexx established its operations in West Chester, Ohio, and targeted a global addressable market that the company estimated at $400 billion across personal care, household products, food, and industrial fluid categories.

The third founding represented a deliberate market-timing call. In 2022, as GPU thermal design powers began approaching the boundaries of air-cooling feasibility at hyperscale data-center densities, Innventure launched Accelsius to commercialize two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling ==sourced under patent and technology agreements with Nokia, whose Bell Labs thermal-management research provided the foundational IP estate==. The technology circulates a dielectric liquid directly onto chip surfaces via a two-phase thermodynamic cycle, achieving heat-dissipation performance that neither conventional air cooling nor single-phase liquid cooling could match at the watt densities that next-generation AI accelerators were beginning to impose. Accelsius completed a $24 million Series A financing to fund early commercial development and built out its NeuCool product family — the IR150 rack-level system rated to 150 kilowatts of cooling capacity, and the multi-rack MR250 scaled to 250 kilowatts — around a core capability demonstrated at 4,500 watts per socket.

## Taking the Platform Public

By 2024, Innventure's operating companies had reached a stage at which the capital requirements of simultaneous early commercialization across three distinct end-markets exceeded what a private holding structure could efficiently sustain. The platform pursued a SPAC merger with Learn CW Investment Corp, structured to bring Innventure itself — rather than any individual operating company — into public capital markets as a consolidated holding entity.

On October 3, 2024, Innventure began trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker INV. The business combination's purchase accounting recognized significant goodwill, establishing consolidated total assets of approximately $905 million — a figure that reflected the assessed value of the platform's three operating companies and their respective technology estates rather than tangible asset holdings. Cash at year-end 2024 stood at $11.1 million against that total-assets base, a disproportion that would become the central financial management challenge of the platform's early public life.

The MATCH scoring framework — evaluating technology opportunities across five dimensions of Market, Advantage, Timeline, Capital, and High Value — and the proprietary DownSelect® due-diligence process managed by SVP of New Company Development Colin Scott were now operating inside a public-company reporting structure for the first time, with quarterly disclosures, audit committee scrutiny, and investor relations obligations that private company-building had not required.

## Refinity and the Fourth Chapter

One month before the end of the platform's first full quarter as a public company, Innventure added a fourth portfolio company. In December 2024, ~~in partnership with~~ ==in collaboration with== The Dow Chemical Company, it founded Refinity to commercialize ==VTT-licensed technology for the== cost-effective conversion of mixed plastic waste streams into chemical intermediates and drop-in petrochemical feedstocks compatible with existing refinery operations. ~~The Dow partnership replicated the structural logic of every prior Innventure founding: a technology developed inside and validated by a major multinational, licensed to a purpose-built operating company, with the MNC retained as a founding commercialization partner whose technical and commercial networks reduced the go-to-market friction that early-stage companies typically absorbed alone.~~ ==The Refinity structure adapted Innventure's playbook to a research-institute sourcing channel: VTT, Finland's state-owned research organization, provided the foundational licensed technology, while Dow served as the collaboration, channel, and commercialization partner whose technical and commercial networks reduced the go-to-market friction that early-stage companies typically absorbed alone.==

With Accelsius, AeroFlexx, and Refinity each at different points on the commercialization curve — Accelsius generating its first commercial revenue in Q3 2024, AeroFlexx shipping its first commercial product deliveries in Q4 2024, and Refinity conducting pilot-scale validation ahead of commercial demonstration plant financing — the platform that Haskell and Otworth assembled from XL TechGroup's institutional memory was, by the frozen snapshot date of May 2026, in the most consequential execution phase of its history.

chapters.title: Three Platforms, Three Markets: NeuCool, Air Assist, and Plastic-to-Chemical — Innventure's Operating Company Portfolio
chapters.body:
## The Physics of Heat at Scale: Accelsius and the NeuCool Platform

At the heart of every AI training cluster sits an engineering problem that chip architects can no longer ignore: the processors running large language models and neural network inference generate heat at densities that conventional cooling architectures cannot sustainably remove. Nvidia's H100 GPU carries a thermal design power of approximately 700 watts; Blackwell-generation accelerators have pushed past 1,000 watts per socket, with roadmap successors expected to exceed 1,500 watts in dense rack configurations. Air cooling — the default thermal management architecture across decades of data-center build-out — reaches a practical ceiling somewhere around 20 to 30 kilowatts per rack. Beyond that threshold, the fluid dynamics of moving air through a rack become thermodynamically impractical: the volume of airflow required to remove heat scales poorly with chip TDP, and the energy consumed by fans begins to represent a meaningful fraction of the total facility power budget.

Accelsius's NeuCool platform ==— built on two-phase cooling patents and technology licensed from Nokia under a 2022 IP and technology agreement —== attacks this problem through two-phase dielectric liquid cooling, a thermodynamic approach that exploits phase change — the conversion of liquid to vapor — as the primary heat-absorption mechanism. In a two-phase system, a dielectric fluid (electrically non-conductive, chemically inert relative to electronics) circulates through cold plates in direct contact with processor surfaces. When the fluid reaches the chip interface, it absorbs enough energy to undergo evaporative phase change at the contact surface; the latent heat of vaporization — the energy required to convert liquid to gas — is dramatically larger than the sensible heat that raising liquid temperature would absorb through the same mass of fluid. The resulting vapor travels to a coolant distribution unit where it condenses back to liquid, releasing that heat to a facility water loop. The thermodynamic cycle then repeats. Because phase change concentrates enormous thermal energy absorption in a thin boundary layer at the chip surface, two-phase direct-to-chip cooling achieves heat flux capacities that single-phase liquid cooling — which relies entirely on temperature differential across the fluid — cannot match without impractical flow rates.

Accelsius demonstrated 4,500 watts per socket under this mechanism, a figure that substantially exceeds the TDP of every current commercially deployed AI accelerator and provides meaningful headroom for anticipated next-generation chip generations through the late 2020s. The significance is not merely that the system works at 4,500 watts today; it is that the physics of two-phase heat transfer allow the same fundamental architecture to scale with chip TDP increases without requiring proportional increases in coolant flow rate, pump energy, or facility infrastructure.

## The NeuCool Product Family

Accelsius translated that thermodynamic capability into two distinct commercial product configurations. The NeuCool IR150 is a fully integrated rack-level solution — an 800 mm-wide enclosure that packages a two-phase coolant distribution unit, 42U of usable IT rack space, and the liquid and vapor manifolds required to close the thermodynamic loop within a single physical unit deployable by a data-center operator without custom fluid-handling infrastructure. The IR150 provides up to 150 kilowatts of cooling capacity per rack, a figure that accommodates current high-density AI accelerator rack configurations and positions the product for several subsequent chip generations without requiring a swap of the cooling infrastructure.

For deployments demanding higher aggregate cooling at the row or cluster level, the NeuCool MR250 is a multi-rack system scaling to 250 kilowatts. The MR250 architecture allows a data-center operator to provision cooling infrastructure ahead of progressive rack densification — a procurement pattern aligned with how hyperscale operators typically phase large campus deployments.

The commercial validation of both product lines arrived at scale with Accelsius's signed partnership with DarkNX for a 300-megawatt AI data-center campus in Ontario, Canada. Management described the DarkNX engagement as the largest publicly disclosed two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling deployment to date — a characterization that, given the nascent state of the market, is simultaneously accurate and a measure of how early the industry inflection point remains. Alongside the DarkNX anchor, Accelsius secured a three-year white-label master purchasing agreement with an unnamed leading global thermal management company, providing a distribution channel into data-center operators whose procurement relationships run through established building infrastructure vendors rather than startup cooling specialists. Johnson Controls and Legrand participated in Accelsius's December 2025 Series B financing at a $665 million post-money valuation; both are strategic investors with existing relationships across the data-center infrastructure supply chain, and their presence signals potential commercial integration pathways beyond pure capital deployment. By early 2026, Accelsius's active sales pipeline exceeded $1 billion in aggregate disclosed opportunities.

## AeroFlexx: Air Assist and the Flexible Packaging Inflection

Procter & Gamble's research organization developed the Air Assist mechanism to address a packaging problem that rigid PET bottles solve inefficiently: creating a self-standing, pour-capable liquid container from flexible film. Conventional flexible pouches collapse under their own weight when partially emptied, making them functionally unsuitable as primary retail packaging for most liquid personal care or household products. P&G's solution was structural: compressed air is used during the filling process to inflate the edges of a flexible film pouch, creating internal air chambers that confer rigidity and allow the package to stand, pour, and be handled like a conventional bottle throughout its use lifecycle.

The engineering consequence of eliminating rigid bottle walls is material reduction at scale. AeroFlexx cited an up to 85 percent reduction in virgin plastic content per unit versus comparable rigid bottles — a claim substantiated by the Association of Plastic Recyclers Critical Guidance certification awarded in May 2025, which validated that the AeroFlexx package is recyclable in streams where plastic bottles are accepted. That certification is commercially significant: without APR recognition, flexible packaging structures are functionally non-recyclable in U.S. municipal recycling infrastructure regardless of their material composition. The June 2025 patent awards deepened the intellectual property moat around the Air Assist mechanism itself, adding to the P&G-derived foundational IP.

The technical differentiation relative to alternatives merits specificity. Conventional spouted pouches collapse as they empty, creating consumer experience failures that have limited their penetration in premium categories. Rigid PET bottles remain the default because they solve the structural problem reliably — but at the cost of substantially higher material use, higher per-unit weight (and therefore higher transportation carbon intensity), and increasingly problematic regulatory exposure as EU Single-Use Plastics Directive implementation and proposed U.S. EPR frameworks create structural headwinds for virgin-plastic packaging at scale.

AeroFlexx's $400 billion total addressable market estimate spans personal care (shampoo, conditioner, body wash, liquid soap), household products (laundry, dish, surface cleaners), food (oils, syrups, condiments), and industrial fluid concentrates. Near-term commercial penetration in personal care and household products offers the most credible near-term volume pathway: both categories are characterized by high purchase frequency, strong brand owner interest in sustainability differentiation, and regulatory pressure that creates genuine CPG procurement urgency. A commercially significant win in personal care — defined as a SKU rollout at a major multinational across a primary line rather than a limited-edition sustainability variant — would require annual volumes in the tens to hundreds of millions of units. The Aveda partnership with Estée Lauder Companies represents a prestige-category proof point; translating it to mass-market household care, where AeroFlexx's environmental economics are most compelling, requires overcoming supply chain inertia in categories where rigid bottle tooling, filling line infrastructure, and retailer shelf specifications have been standardized for decades. The Chemipack European manufacturing collaboration establishes an initial Continental production footprint to support EU market approaches.

## Refinity: The Plastic-to-Chemical Conversion Platform

Refinity, founded in December 2024 ~~through Innventure's partnership with The Dow Chemical Company~~ ==around plastic-to-chemical conversion technology licensed from Finland's VTT Technical Research Centre, with The Dow Chemical Company joining as collaboration, channel, and commercialization partner==, operates at the feedstock end of the plastics value chain. The company's process converts mixed plastic waste streams — materials that are too heterogeneous or contaminated for mechanical recycling — into chemical intermediates and drop-in petrochemical feedstocks suitable for direct substitution in existing ethylene crackers and petrochemical plant operations without process modification.

The "drop-in" designation carries specific technical meaning: the output hydrocarbon streams must meet the compositional specifications of conventional naphtha or other cracker feeds so that operators can blend or substitute them without equipment changes, co-processing permits, or reformulation of downstream polymer products. Achieving drop-in compatibility with mixed-plastic inputs requires pyrolysis or catalytic conversion processes capable of managing the heterogeneous feedstock variability that makes mixed plastic waste streams commercially attractive (low cost, abundant, with landfill trajectory that creates regulatory incentive for diversion) but technically demanding. Refinery pilot-scale validation has been completed; commercial demonstration plant financing and construction represent the next milestone.

Dow Chemical's involvement is ~~both technically and commercially~~ ==primarily commercially== significant. As one of the world's largest ethylene producers, Dow operates cracker infrastructure that represents a natural commercial pathway for Refinity's output streams — existing plant capacity, existing offtake infrastructure, and existing commercial relationships with the polymer producers who would ultimately consume recycled-content feedstock. ==The underlying conversion chemistry, however, traces to VTT's research program rather than Dow's R&D portfolio.== Refinity's technology readiness level sits at pilot-validated, pre-commercial-demonstration — the earliest stage among Innventure's three active portfolio companies, with a timeline to meaningful revenue measured in years rather than quarters.

## PureCycle as Lineage: The Repeatable Template

PureCycle Technologies — the solvent-based polypropylene purification venture Innventure founded in 2015 around a P&G Research Fellow's recycling process — completed a SPAC IPO on Nasdaq in March 2021 at a valuation exceeding $1 billion, and is no longer part of Innventure's consolidated financials. Its relevance to the current portfolio is not accounting but epistemological: PureCycle demonstrated that Innventure's methodology — licensing dormant corporate IP, constructing a purpose-built operating company, funding through early commercialization, and accessing public markets before reaching cash-flow break-even — can produce a billion-dollar enterprise from a technology that P&G had developed but not itself commercialized. Whether Accelsius, AeroFlexx, or Refinity replicates that outcome remains unresolved, but PureCycle's trajectory is the single most informative data point for calibrating the probability distribution.

## A Portfolio United by Constraint

The most striking feature of Innventure's operating company portfolio is not the diversity of its end markets — data-center cooling, flexible packaging, and chemical feedstock conversion address structurally distinct customer bases — but the unity of its underlying commercial logic. Accelsius, AeroFlexx, and Refinity each target the sustainability, resource efficiency, and infrastructure decarbonization megatrend through technologies that substitute resource-intensive incumbent solutions with capital-efficient, lower-footprint alternatives. Each also faces the same three-part commercialization constraint: the need for patient capital to sustain pre-revenue or pre-scale operations through extended procurement cycles, the reality that hyperscaler and CPG procurement decisions operate on timelines that rarely accommodate startup capital structures, and the operational complexity of executing three simultaneous company builds from a 169-person organization. That tension — between the asymmetric optionality embedded in three potentially billion-dollar platforms and the compounding burn of building them simultaneously — defines Innventure's investment proposition as of the May 2026 snapshot.

chapters.title: A Balance Sheet Built on Goodwill: Revenue, Impairment, and the Road to Commercial Scale
chapters.body:
## The Structural Anomaly

Any analyst approaching Innventure's financials for the first time confronts an immediate arithmetic dissonance. At December 31, 2024 — the first balance-sheet date after the company's October 3 listing on the Nasdaq Global Market — [total assets stood at $905.3 million](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002001557/000162828025017614/innv-20241231.htm). Yet cash on hand was $11.1 million, and consolidated net revenue for the full fiscal year totalled $1.22 million. The gap between those figures is not a rounding error or a presentation artefact. It is the defining feature of purchase accounting applied to a SPAC business combination — and understanding it is a prerequisite to interpreting anything else Innventure reports.

When Learn CW Investment Corp and Innventure LLC closed their business combination, generally accepted accounting principles required the surviving entity to mark the acquired assets and liabilities to fair value at the transaction date. The excess of the purchase price over the fair value of identifiable net assets is recognised as goodwill. For Innventure, whose operating companies were pre-revenue or barely-revenue ventures holding technology licences, assembled workforces, and unproven commercial pipelines, the identifiable intangible asset base was inherently speculative — and goodwill absorbed the remainder. The result was a balance sheet whose $905.3 million asset total was, in the most literal sense, a capitalised expression of what investors believed the platform's future cash flows might be worth at the moment the deal closed.

Cash was a different matter. Eleven million dollars against three operating companies, a 169-person workforce, and an overhead structure spread across Orlando, West Chester, and multiple data-centre deployment sites left almost no margin for operational delay.

## FY2024: The First Consolidated Year

The [FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002001557/000162828025017614/innv-20241231.htm) presents a structurally unusual income statement. Because the SPAC transaction closed on October 2, 2024, GAAP required Innventure to split its annual report into a Predecessor period (January 1 through October 1) and a Successor period (October 2 through December 31). Period-over-period comparisons are therefore technically non-equivalent, and reconstructing a clean twelve-month operating-cost trajectory requires aggregating both segments — a complexity that the company's management and its two covering analysts have had to navigate explicitly.

On a combined-period basis, consolidated net revenue for fiscal 2024 totalled $1.22 million. Accelsius contributed the inaugural figure: its first commercial NeuCool system was delivered to a paying customer in the third quarter of 2024, making that deployment the platform's initial product revenue event. AeroFlexx began commercial shipments of its flexible liquid-packaging systems in the fourth quarter, adding a secondary revenue line. Refinity, having been founded only in December 2024, generated nothing. No granular revenue-by-subsidiary breakdown was publicly disclosed at the time of writing, but the chronology of commercial milestones implies Accelsius was the dominant contributor to FY2024 revenue, with AeroFlexx representing an early and partial quarter's contribution.

Gross margin disclosure was limited. Operating expenses on a combined-period basis drove a reported operating loss of $76.8 million. General and administrative expense — encompassing the corporate holding-company overhead as well as operating-company management costs — represented the largest recurring cash line. Research and development allocations across Accelsius and AeroFlexx were separately identified but not granularly disaggregated in summary press-release disclosures. Stock-based compensation, a non-cash charge typical of SPAC-era management incentive structures, was a meaningful component of total reported expense. The $98.8 million net loss exceeded the $76.8 million operating loss primarily because of financing and transaction-related costs absorbed through the SPAC close.

[Adjusted EBITDA for FY2024 was negative $27.9 million](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/04/11/3059994/0/en/Innventure-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2024-Results.html), stripping out stock-based compensation, depreciation and amortisation on acquired intangibles, and non-recurring transaction costs. The adjusted figure is useful precisely because it excludes the SPAC accounting noise — but it still represents approximately $27.9 million of real cash leaving the business annually on recurring operational activity. Divided across twelve months, that implies a quarterly cash-consumption rate of roughly $7 million before any capital-raise proceeds, a figure consistent with the scale of the workforce and the early-deployment capex required to install NeuCool systems at customer sites.

## Q1 2025: The Impairment Quarter

If FY2024 established the platform's financial baseline, the first quarter of 2025 delivered its most consequential single financial event since listing. Management disclosed a $233.2 million goodwill impairment charge for the period ending March 31, 2025 — a write-down that, in a single reporting quarter, nearly tripled the scale of the full-year 2024 net loss.

Under GAAP, goodwill is tested for impairment at least annually — and whenever a triggering event indicates that the carrying amount of a reporting unit may exceed its fair value. The most common triggering event for public companies is a sustained decline in market capitalisation below book value. Innventure's share price had retreated materially from its post-listing levels as the market digested the gap between the $905 million asset base and $1.22 million in actual revenue. When market capitalisation falls below the equity book value, auditors and management are required to test whether the implied fair value of each reporting unit still supports its recorded goodwill. For Innventure, it did not — and $233.2 million was written off.

The financial consequences were immediate and compounding. The reported net loss for Q1 2025 reached [$253.7 million](https://ir.innventure.com/news-releases/news-release-details/innventure-reports-first-quarter-2025-results) — a quarterly figure that dwarfed the entire prior fiscal year's loss. Cash fell from $11.1 million at year-end 2024 to approximately $1.4 million by the end of March 2025. At that level, the consolidated entity had roughly weeks, not quarters, of operating runway remaining. Innventure's auditors issued a going-concern qualification in the FY2024 10-K, a standard accounting signal that the entity's ability to continue as a going concern was in substantial doubt absent additional financing.

The response was a $40 million registered direct offering completed in January 2026, pricing shares and warrants in a transaction that ~~restored operating runway but added dilution to existing shareholders at a moment when the stock was trading well below its original SPAC listing range~~ ==improved liquidity and added dilution to existing shareholders at a moment when the stock was trading well below its original SPAC listing range, but did not extinguish the underlying going-concern or capital-access risk==. Critically, ~~goodwill remaining on the balance sheet after the Q1 2025 write-down still carries impairment risk if the stock price or business-unit valuations deteriorate further — a structural overhang that will follow the company into each subsequent reporting period.~~ ==additional goodwill impairment followed later in FY2025, bringing the full-year write-down to $346.6 million; the remaining goodwill balance continues to carry impairment risk if the stock price or business-unit valuations deteriorate further, a structural overhang that will follow the company into each subsequent reporting period.==

## FY2025 and the Capital Formation Strategy

Full-year 2025 revenue reached approximately [$2.06 million](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/INV/innventure-reports-first-quarter-2025-rosg98ypqgku.html) — a 69 percent year-over-year increase that, while operationally meaningful, continues to describe a pre-scale enterprise by any conventional metric. Accelsius's expanding NeuCool deployment base and AeroFlexx's continued commercial shipments drove the incremental revenue. The net loss for FY2025 was approximately ~~$171 million — lower on a reported basis than the Q1 2025 quarter alone, reflecting the non-recurrence of the $233.2 million impairment charge as the dominant driver rather than any underlying operating improvement~~ ==$475.4 million on a total basis, or $293.3 million attributable to Innventure stockholders — higher than the Q1 2025 quarter alone, reflecting additional goodwill impairment recognised after Q1 that brought the full-year write-down to $346.6 million, alongside continued operating-cost intensity==. Adjusted for non-cash items, recurring cash consumption remained substantial==, with FY2025 adjusted EBITDA disclosed at negative $78.8 million==.

| Metric | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Net revenue | $1.22M | ~$2.06M |
| YoY revenue growth | n/a (first full year) | ~69% |
| Operating loss | $76.8M | ~~n/a (not yet fully disclosed)~~ ==Disclosed in Q4/FY2025 release (includes $346.6M full-year goodwill impairment)== |
| Net loss | $98.8M | ~~$171M~~ ==$475.4M total / $293.3M attributable== |
| Adjusted EBITDA | -$27.9M | ~~Not disclosed~~ ==-$78.8M== |
| Cash at period-end | $11.1M | ~~$1.4M (Q1 2025) → restored by RDO~~ ==$1.4M was the Q1 2025 cash trough, not the FY2025 period-end figure; January 2026 $40M RDO added subsequent liquidity== |

With approximately ~~$27–30 million in annualised cash burn at the adjusted level~~ ==FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of negative $78.8 million and Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of negative $18.4 million implying an annualised burn pace closer to $74 million== and a $40 million RDO completed in January 2026, the implied runway — assuming stable burn and no operating-company cash inflows — extended to ~~roughly four to six quarters~~ ==roughly six to seven months== from the close of that offering, depending on the timing and scale of Accelsius system deployments. Any meaningful Accelsius revenue recognised in 2026 — management guided for cash-flow positivity at the Accelsius subsidiary level by year-end 2026 — would extend that runway materially, but the margin for error remains thin.

## Capital Structure and Dilution Dynamics

Innventure's capital architecture is notable for ~~what it lacks as much as what it contains. [No material long-term debt appears in available public filings](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/04/3249263/0/en/Innventure-Operating-Companies-Advance-to-Independent-Capital-Formation-as-Platform-Momentum-Accelerates.html). The company is funded almost entirely through equity at both the holding-company and operating-company levels — a structure that insulates the consolidated entity from debt-service risk but concentrates all financing pressure on the equity markets.~~ ==its layered capital structure across the holding company and operating subsidiaries. [Public filings disclose material debt and debt-like obligations at December 31, 2025](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/04/3249263/0/en/Innventure-Operating-Companies-Advance-to-Independent-Capital-Formation-as-Platform-Momentum-Accelerates.html), even as equity has been the dominant funding source at both the holding-company and operating-company levels. The equity markets bear most ongoing financing pressure alongside the consolidated entity's disclosed debt-service obligations.==

At the operating-company level, Accelsius raised a $24 million Series A and closed a Series B in December 2025 with strategic investors Johnson Controls International and Legrand at a post-money valuation of $665 million. AeroFlexx and Refinity were pursuing direct capital raises at the time of the snapshot, targeting investors who would serve simultaneously as commercial distribution partners. With approximately 84 million shares outstanding, each independent raise at the subsidiary level introduces structural complexity: if Accelsius, for instance, continues raising capital at valuations that grow independently of INV's consolidated market capitalisation — currently approximately $536 million — the holding company's ownership percentage dilutes while the subsidiary's implied value may grow. INV shareholders bear dilution at the parent level without a proportionate economic pass-through unless the platform retains sufficient controlling equity at each operating company.

## Benchmarking the Profile

Innventure occupies an unusual position in the public-market landscape. Its GICS classification as an asset-management entity understates the operational intensity of running three technology ventures simultaneously. The most useful comparisons operate at two levels.

At the platform level, IP Group plc — the London-listed university spinout commercialiser — offers the closest structural analogue: a holding company that incubates early-stage technology ventures, funds them through equity, and seeks exits via IPO or trade sale. IP Group's early years showed comparable revenue-to-asset ratios and similar dependence on ongoing equity raises before portfolio companies matured.

At the Accelsius subsidiary level, Vertiv Holdings (VRT) and Modine Manufacturing (MOD) represent scaled incumbents in data-centre thermal management against which Accelsius's revenue trajectory will ultimately be measured. Vertiv generated approximately $7 billion in revenue in fiscal 2024; Modine's data-centre segment contributed roughly $1.5 billion. Accelsius — at sub-$10 million annualised revenue as of early 2026 — is years from those scales, but the market is pricing it on the trajectory rather than the current run rate.

The AeroFlexx analogue is more challenging to construct. Amcor plc (AMCR) and Berry Global (BERY) are packaging incumbents with billions in revenue and entrenched customer relationships that AeroFlexx must displace over multi-year sales cycles.

## Financial Milestones That Would Matter

The specific financial outcomes that would materially alter Innventure's forward narrative are identifiable. Accelsius achieving a quarterly revenue run rate — management guided for cash-flow positivity at the subsidiary level by year-end 2026 — that demonstrates a clear path to covering its own operating costs would remove the subsidiary from the consolidated cash-burn calculation and provide the platform's first genuine proof point since PureCycle's 2021 IPO. AeroFlexx securing a disclosed mid-tier CPG anchor customer beyond Aveda — a household or personal care brand with global volume commitments — would validate the packaging technology's commercial scalability and reduce the binary risk concentration in a single prestige-brand reference.

Any change to the going-concern qualification status — whether resolved in the subsequent FY2025 audit or in an interim quarterly review — would represent a material improvement in the company's creditworthiness and equity narrative. And the financing of Refinity's commercial demonstration plant, when it occurs, will establish an independent market-based valuation for the third portfolio company for the first time, providing a concrete data point for what the ~~Dow Chemical partnership~~ ==VTT-licensed technology with Dow as commercialization and channel partner== is commercially worth. Until those milestones accumulate, Innventure's balance sheet remains what it was at inception: a capitalised wager, carefully structured in GAAP, on the proposition that dormant corporate science can be made commercially formidable.

chapters.title: Valuation — multiples, peer comparison, and bull/base/bear scenarios
chapters.body:
## Pricing a Platform That Has Almost Nothing to Price

Innventure's valuation problem is unusual even by the tolerant standards of early-stage industrials. With consolidated net revenue of approximately $2.06 million for fiscal 2025 against a market capitalization of roughly $536 million — derived from approximately 84 million shares outstanding at a price around $6.38 as of late May 2026 — the stock's conventional multiples are not merely elevated but effectively undefined. Trailing price-to-earnings is not meaningful (the company posted a ~~net loss of approximately $171 million in 2025~~ ==net loss attributable to Innventure stockholders of approximately $293.3 million for fiscal 2025, on a total consolidated net loss of $475.4 million==). EV/EBITDA is similarly inapplicable; ~~adjusted EBITDA for 2024 was negative $27.9 million, and the 2025 figure incorporates the $233.2 million goodwill impairment that reduced per-share book value materially~~ ==FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was negative $78.8 million, and the consolidated 2025 result also absorbed $346.6 million of goodwill impairment that reduced per-share book value materially==. The one ratio that produces a number — enterprise value to trailing revenue — comes to approximately 260 times fiscal 2025 sales, a figure that communicates the pre-scale nature of the enterprise rather than any structural insight. Price-to-book, by contrast, ~~is closer to par: after the impairment, residual stockholders' equity stood in the low-to-mid-$500 million range, placing P/B near 1.0 times — an anchor that tells investors only that the market has not yet chosen to bid the equity above its written-down book basis~~ ==tells a different story: Innventure, Inc. stockholders' equity stood at $204.2 million at December 31, 2025, placing P/B near 2.6 times — an anchor that signals the market is already paying a meaningful premium to the written-down book basis for the platform's intangible optionality==.

The stock's 52-week range of $2.36 to $7.86 brackets the analytical problem neatly. At the trough, the equity implied deep skepticism about near-term capital availability; at the peak, it reflected optimism about Accelsius's commercial momentum following the December 2025 Series B close. Neither end of that range was anchored by earnings or cash-flow-based valuation — both were driven by news events and sentiment shifts around a company whose intrinsic value is almost entirely lodged in the probability-weighted optionality of three operating subsidiaries converting technology licenses into commercial franchises.

## Peer-Group Context and the Limits of Comparison

Building a workable peer table for Innventure requires treating the holding company and its operating subsidiaries as conceptually distinct objects. At the platform level, the closest publicly listed analogue is [IP Group plc](https://www.ipgroupplc.com/) (LSE: IPO), a London-listed technology commercialization vehicle that takes equity stakes in spinouts from UK universities and corporate research programs. IP Group trades at a persistent discount to reported net asset value — typically 0.55 to 0.70 times NAV — reflecting the market's standard skepticism about holding-company structures that interpose an additional layer of overhead and governance between investors and the underlying assets. Innventure's ~~1.0~~ ==roughly 2.6== times book-value pricing is therefore ~~not obviously cheap by that standard; it implies the market is not applying the discount typically levied on IP-type vehicles, possibly because the equity base was so recently reset by the goodwill impairment~~ ==at a clear premium to that benchmark; the market is paying well above the written-down equity base rather than applying the discount typically levied on IP-type vehicles, a stance that places the entire burden of justification on subsidiary execution==.

At the Accelsius subsidiary level, the most relevant comparables are Vertiv Holdings (NASDAQ: VRT) and Modine Manufacturing (NYSE: MOD), both of which have built substantial data-center thermal management franchises. For sustainable packaging, Amcor plc (NYSE: AMCR) and Berry Global Group (NYSE: BERY) serve as the mature-incumbent reference points for what AeroFlexx aspires to enter. The table below presents approximate multiples as of the frozen snapshot.

| Company | Ticker | EV/Sales (NTM) | EV/EBITDA (NTM) | P/E (NTM) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Innventure Inc. | INV | ~260× (trailing) | N/M | N/M | Pre-revenue; multiples reflect option value |
| Vertiv Holdings | VRT | ~3–4× | ~22–26× | ~35–42× | Scaled data-center infrastructure; high-growth re-rating |
| Modine Manufacturing | MOD | ~1.5–2× | ~12–15× | ~18–22× | Data-center cooling fast-growing segment |
| Amcor plc | AMCR | ~1.2–1.4× | ~9–11× | ~14–17× | Scaled flexible packaging; mature margins |
| Berry Global Group | BERY | ~0.9–1.1× | ~7–9× | ~10–13× | Rigid and flexible packaging; leveraged buyout lineage |
| IP Group plc | IPO.L | ~0.6–0.7× NAV | N/M | N/M | Technology commercialization; UK-listed; persistent NAV discount |

The gap between INV and its operational comparables is not irrational — it reflects the standard pre-revenue premium assigned to businesses whose potential is real but whose conversion to cash flow is uncertain and multi-year. What is notable is that if Accelsius alone achieves Vertiv-level scale — say, $500 million in annual revenue at a 3.5 times EV/Sales multiple — the implied enterprise value of that single subsidiary approaches $1.75 billion, a figure materially larger than Innventure's current consolidated market capitalization. The analytical exercise that follows attempts to assign probabilities to that path.

## What Accelsius Embeds in the Current Price

The December 2025 Series B placed Accelsius at a $665 million post-money valuation with Johnson Controls and Legrand as strategic co-investors. ~~Innventure's ownership stake post-Series B has not been precisely quantified in public filings as of the snapshot date, but given the structure of early-stage holding companies that retain majority positions through first and second financing rounds, a working assumption of 55 to 65 percent INV ownership implies an attributable Accelsius value to INV of approximately $365 million to $430 million. Against a consolidated market capitalization of $536 million, that range suggests AeroFlexx, Refinity, and the platform overhead are being valued collectively in a range of roughly $105 million to $170 million — or potentially at near-zero if the market is implicitly discounting the holding-company overhead against the subsidiary stakes.~~ ==Innventure's economic ownership of Accelsius runs to approximately 43.2 percent following the Series B, implying an attributable Accelsius value to INV of approximately $287 million before holding-company adjustments. Against a consolidated market capitalization of $536 million, that figure suggests AeroFlexx, Refinity, and the platform overhead are being valued collectively at roughly $249 million — a meaningful residual that the market still assigns to the broader portfolio after the Accelsius stake.==

The implied message from current pricing is that the market believes Accelsius is worth ~~something — perhaps $300 to $400 million of the consolidated equity value — while assigning relatively modest probability-weighted value to the other two operating companies. That pricing is not necessarily wrong, but it is notable: it means a buyer of INV at current prices acquires AeroFlexx and Refinity optionality at minimal incremental cost above the Accelsius stake~~ ==roughly $287 million of the consolidated equity value, with a comparably sized residual carrying AeroFlexx, Refinity, and platform overhead. That pricing is not necessarily wrong, but it is notable: it means a buyer of INV at current prices is paying nearly as much for the non-Accelsius portfolio and the holding-company superstructure as for the Accelsius stake itself==. The counter-argument is that corporate overhead, dilution from future subsidiary capital raises, and the structural complexity of the holding company consume a portion of the apparent embedded value.

## Three Scenarios: Bull, Base, and Bear

**Bull case — Accelsius delivers, portfolio compounds.** The $1 billion-plus active sales pipeline converts to signed contracts at a clip consistent with management's guidance for Accelsius cash-flow positivity by year-end 2026. DarkNX's 300-megawatt Ontario campus becomes the reference deployment that unlocks a second and third hyperscale customer. The white-label master purchasing agreement provides volume production economics that drive unit costs below air-cooling alternatives for high-TDP applications. By end of 2027, Accelsius reaches a $200 million annualized revenue run-rate. At a 6 times EV/Sales multiple — a moderate premium to Vertiv's current trading level, justified by higher growth — Accelsius commands a $1.2 billion enterprise value. INV's ~~60~~ ==43.2== percent stake implies approximately ~~$720~~ ==$518== million attributable value. Adding a conservative $150 million for AeroFlexx (which by this scenario has secured two or three additional prestige CPG brands beyond Aveda) and negligible credit for Refinity, then deducting platform overhead and applying a 15 percent holding-company discount, produces a per-share value in the range of ~~$14 to $18~~ ==$10 to $13==. ~~The two-analyst consensus price target of $14.50 sits at the low end of this range, suggesting the street's bull case is itself conservative.~~ ==The two-analyst consensus price target of $14.50 sits above the top of this range, suggesting the street is pricing in execution at least as strong as this dossier's bull case contemplates.==

**Base case — gradual progress, constrained capital.** Accelsius converts a portion of the pipeline but faces elongated enterprise sales cycles and deployment complexity at hyperscale sites. Revenue reaches $75 million by end of 2027, generating sufficient cash for operational independence but not yet demonstrating the repeatability required for premium multiple assignment. At 4 times EV/Sales, Accelsius is valued at $300 million. INV's stake yields approximately ~~$180~~ ==$130== million of attributable value. AeroFlexx achieves $20 to $30 million in revenue but requires continued capital support. Consolidated INV equity value, after holding-company costs and dilution, settles in the ~~$8 to $11~~ ==$7 to $10== per share range — modest upside from current levels but well short of analyst targets.

**Bear case — capital exhaustion and competitive displacement.** Hyperscale operators slow direct-to-chip liquid-cooling adoption as next-generation air-cooling configurations improve, or consolidate cooling procurement with Vertiv and established OEM incumbents who move faster than anticipated into two-phase solutions. Accelsius's pipeline extends without converting, burning cash through 2026 and requiring a down-round or distressed financing that dilutes INV materially. AeroFlexx fails to move past the pilot-brand stage. Corporate overhead compounds the losses. In a forced-equity or partial-liquidation scenario, INV shares fall back toward the 52-week trough of $2.36, implying total equity value around $200 million — essentially a write-down of the Accelsius Series B premium with minimal residual value attributed to the other assets.

## The Consensus Gap and the Dossier's Read

The two-analyst consensus of $14.50 implies 127 percent upside from the late-May 2026 price. That target is ~~arithmetically consistent with the bull case but requires~~ ==arithmetically above even this dossier's bull case and requires== Accelsius to convert meaningfully from its pipeline within a twelve- to eighteen-month window. What the consensus may be underweighting is the structural complexity of deploying two-phase liquid cooling at 300-megawatt scale — projects that involve not merely component procurement but facility redesign, coolant distribution infrastructure, and long procurement cycles inside organizations whose capital allocation is already under scrutiny.

The dossier's read differs ~~modestly~~ ==more sharply== from the consensus: Accelsius's $665 million Series B valuation, anchored by credible strategic investors with direct data-center market relationships, provides genuine support for the thesis — but the holding-company discount, the dilution mechanics of three concurrent capital-raise processes, and the going-concern history argue for a wider distribution of outcomes than a single strong-buy target implies. The current price near $6.38 is not obviously expensive given that Accelsius alone was valued at a substantial premium to consolidated INV equity just six months prior. It is, however, a price that demands Accelsius execution above almost any other variable — making the DarkNX deployment timeline and the white-label OEM order cadence the two most consequential data points in the next four quarters.

chapters.title: Quarters at the Frontier: Management Commentary and the Commercial Inflection Narrative
chapters.body:
## The First Product Dollar

When Accelsius delivered its inaugural NeuCool system to a commercial data-center customer during the third quarter of 2024, the transaction was modest by any conventional measure. The counterparty was unnamed, the system size undisclosed beyond the product's rack-level specification, and the revenue contribution — absorbed into the $1.22 million consolidated total that would constitute Innventure's entire reported full-year 2024 net revenue — was a rounding error against the platform's operating losses. Yet the delivery carried an outsized narrative weight: it was the first time a dollar had moved from a paying customer to an Accelsius invoice, transforming the two-phase direct-to-chip cooling technology from a validated laboratory claim into a commercial asset. [Innventure FY2024 10-K via SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002001557/000162828025017614/innv-20241231.htm)

Management chose not to name the initial customer or specify the precise system deployed, a pattern of commercial disclosure that would persist through subsequent quarters and frustrate investors seeking anchor-customer confirmation. Accelsius's first deployment corresponded with the period immediately preceding the October 3, 2024 SPAC close — making it both a commercial inflection and a pre-listing proof point that the platform's commercialization model had graduated from incubation to execution.

## "A Seminal Year": The Full-Year 2024 Framing

On April 11, 2025, Innventure filed an 8-K attaching the press release reporting fourth-quarter and full-year 2024 results. CEO Bill Haskell opened with a statement that set the template for how management would narrate the gap between financial reality and commercial ambition:

> "2024 was a seminal year for Innventure, highlighted by commercial delivery of product for both Accelsius and AeroFlexx, the October close of our business combination and subsequent public listing, and the launch of our fourth operating company, Refinity."

[Innventure FY2024 Earnings Release, GlobeNewsWire, April 11, 2025](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/04/11/3059994/0/en/Innventure-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2024-Results.html)

The framing was defensible on its own terms: each of the cited milestones was real. But the financial statements that accompanied the release complicated the narrative considerably. Consolidated net revenue for the full year was $1.22 million. The net loss was $98.8 million. Operating cash had contracted to $11.1 million at December 31, 2024 — the balance sheet's headline $905.3 million total-asset figure having been almost entirely constituted by goodwill and acquisition-related intangibles recognized in the October business combination. The adjusted EBITDA loss of $27.9 million, the cleanest measure of recurring cash consumption, implied that at prevailing burn rates the company had roughly twelve to fifteen months of liquidity without additional financing.

| Metric | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Net Revenue | $1.22M | ~$2.06M |
| Net Loss | $98.8M | ~~$171M~~ ==$475.4M total / $293.3M attributable to INV stockholders== |
| Adjusted EBITDA | –$27.9M | ~~n/d~~ ==–$78.8M== |
| Cash at Period End | $11.1M | ~~$1.4M (Q1 2025 low)~~ ==Q1 2025 trough of ~$1.4M (Mar 31, 2025), not FY2025 period-end== |
| Shares Outstanding | — | ~84M |

The word "seminal" — implying formative, consequential — was accurate in a structural sense. The commercial deliveries of Q3 and Q4 2024 did establish proof of revenue generation. But the magnitude of the operating loss against a sub-million-dollar revenue base underscored that the platform had not yet crossed any threshold that would alter its fundamental dependency on equity markets.

## The Impairment Quarter: Q1 2025

The first quarter of 2025 produced the most consequential single disclosure in Innventure's short public history. A $233.2 million goodwill impairment — the largest non-cash charge the company had recorded ==up to that point== — drove Q1 2025 net loss to $253.7 million, nearly three times the entire full-year 2024 loss in a single quarter. ==Additional impairment recognized later in the year would lift cumulative FY2025 goodwill impairment to $346.6 million.== Cash at the operating-company level fell to approximately $1.4 million, levels that prompted Innventure's auditors to include a going-concern qualification in the FY2024 10-K, a disclosure that management was obliged to highlight in subsequent SEC filings and investor communications. [Innventure Q1 2025 Earnings Release, Innventure IR](https://ir.innventure.com/news-releases/news-release-details/innventure-reports-first-quarter-2025-results)

Management's explanation of the impairment methodology was important context. The write-down reflected a reassessment of the fair-value assumptions embedded in the October 2024 SPAC purchase accounting — specifically, a reduction in projected near-term revenue ramp rates and a market-capitalization-based cross-check that, at prevailing INV share prices in early 2025, indicated the carrying value of goodwill exceeded recoverable amounts. The impairment was a mark-to-market reckoning on the gap between the SPAC deal's implied valuation and what the public equity market was ascribing to the platform on a day-to-day basis.

Yet even in this operationally sobering quarter, Haskell maintained the commercial optimism that had characterized the April earnings release. Management's commentary described Accelsius as possessing "market leading technology" in two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling and expressed explicit "confidence in achieving revenue growth inflection during the second half of 2025." The H2 2025 inflection thesis rested on Accelsius converting an active pipeline — which management had framed as exceeding $1 billion — into sequential, billable deployments. The going-concern qualification was acknowledged; the response, management indicated, would be found in accelerating operating-company commercialization and, if necessary, accessing capital markets again.

## The H2 2025 Test

The degree to which the H2 2025 inflection materialized is reflected most clearly in the full-year 2025 revenue figure: approximately $2.06 million, representing a 69 percent year-over-year increase over the $1.22 million reported for 2024. The growth rate is real; the absolute scale is not transformative. Against a management narrative that had framed H2 2025 as a commercial inflection point, the annual revenue outcome placed the platform in the uncomfortable position of having grown — but not inflected in any sense that reduced near-term capital risk.

The ~~net loss for FY2025 of approximately $171 million compared favorably to the $98.8 million FY2024 loss only in the narrow sense that the prior year included SPAC-related non-cash charges that did not recur~~ ==FY2025 net loss of approximately $475 million on a total basis — $293 million attributable to Innventure, Inc. common stockholders — substantially exceeded the $98.8 million FY2024 loss, driven by $346.6 million of cumulative goodwill impairment recognized during the year and a deepening adjusted-EBITDA loss of $78.8 million==. The underlying operating cost structure ~~did not meaningfully compress~~ ==did not compress; on an adjusted-EBITDA basis the recurring burn nearly tripled year-on-year==. The platform's funded runway was effectively exhausted entering 2026 without additional capital — a dynamic that forced management's hand before the fiscal year closed.

## The Capital Lifeline and the Series B Signal

Two transactions in late 2025 and early 2026 reset the liquidity narrative. In December 2025, Accelsius completed a fully funded Series B financing with strategic investors Johnson Controls International and Legrand at a post-money valuation of $665 million — a figure that, standing alone, exceeded the consolidated INV market capitalization of approximately $536 million as of late May 2026. The participation of two infrastructure-oriented industrials as strategic co-investors was interpreted by analysts as more than a financial event: Johnson Controls's data-center services footprint and Legrand's building infrastructure distribution provide plausible commercial amplification pathways for NeuCool system sales beyond Accelsius's direct sales force. Management guided Accelsius toward cash-flow positivity by year-end 2026. [Innventure March 2026 Corporate Update, GlobeNewsWire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/04/3249263/0/en/Innventure-Operating-Companies-Advance-to-Independent-Capital-Formation-as-Platform-Momentum-Accelerates.html)

In January 2026, Innventure itself completed a $40 million registered direct offering at the holding-company level, ~~restoring platform operating runway and extinguishing the going-concern risk that had shadowed the balance sheet since the Q1 2025 impairment~~ ==restoring near-term platform operating runway and materially improving liquidity, though without fully extinguishing the going-concern and capital-access risks that had shadowed the balance sheet since the Q1 2025 impairment — Innventure also carried material debt and debt-like obligations at December 31, 2025, leaving the platform reliant on continued capital-markets access==. The offering was dilutive to existing INV shareholders — adding to an already dilution-heavy capital trajectory — but it bought the platform the runway its three operating companies needed to reach the commercial inflection that H2 2025 had not fully delivered.

## The $50 Million Bookings Announcement

The Q1 2026 corporate update, released in March 2026, delivered the most commercially concrete disclosure since listing: aggregate bookings exceeding $50 million across Innventure's operating companies, the highest quarterly commercial traction figure the platform had reported. The announcement was accompanied by two named-customer disclosures that gave the bookings number tangible anchoring.

Accelsius announced a signed partnership with DarkNX for a 300-megawatt AI data-center campus in Ontario, Canada — described as the largest publicly disclosed two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling deployment to date. AeroFlexx simultaneously announced a global commercial partnership with Aveda, an Estée Lauder Companies brand, establishing the first prestige beauty adoption of the Air Assist flexible packaging technology.

The critical analytical question around the $50 million bookings figure is conversion quality. Management's disclosure did not explicitly distinguish between binding purchase orders with committed delivery schedules and pipeline commitments or letters of intent — a distinction that matters materially for revenue recognition timing. The DarkNX partnership is the most visible individual commitment, but a 300-megawatt campus buildout is a multi-year infrastructure program whose NeuCool system deliveries will be phased over an extended deployment cycle. The booking-to-revenue conversion cadence has not been precisely disclosed, leaving analysts to rely on the Accelsius cash-flow-positivity-by-year-end-2026 guidance as the primary timing anchor.

What the Q1 2026 bookings figure does confirm — and what the prior seven quarters of management commentary had been building toward — is that Accelsius's pipeline is converting from verbal engagement to commercial paper. Whether the $50 million represents the first installment of a durable quarterly commercial run-rate or a concentrated front-loading of the longest-gestating opportunities in the funnel is the question that the subsequent two quarters of 2026 will answer.

chapters.title: The Founders Who Built PureCycle and the Team They Assembled to Do It Again
chapters.body:
## The Methodologist and the Architect

The company that became Innventure was built around a thesis developed over two decades: that large corporations systematically underutilize their best science, and that a small, purpose-built team of company-builders can unlock that dormant value faster than either the corporation itself or a conventional venture fund. Understanding Innventure's leadership means understanding the two men who assembled that thesis — and assessing whether the team they have built around them can execute it simultaneously across three operating companies.

## Bill Haskell: Company-Builder by Design

Bill Haskell arrived at Iowa State University to study engineering and stayed long enough to complete post-graduate work in applied mathematics — a combination that shaped a professional identity as a systems-level problem-solver rather than a single-domain technologist. His first decade out of Iowa State was spent on space-borne imaging platforms, the kind of precision-engineering environment that rewards analytical rigor and punishes assumptions. That technical foundation is consequential: Haskell's role at Innventure is not to master the chemistry of polypropylene recycling or the thermodynamics of two-phase liquid cooling, but to construct and operate the organizational scaffolding that converts licensed intellectual property into funded, staffed, revenue-generating companies.

His transition from engineering to company-building began in 1993 with the co-founding of XL Vision, where he served as president through 1999. XL Vision was an early-stage platform for technology commercialization aligned with what would become the XL TechGroup methodology. When XL TechGroup itself was formalized in 2001, Haskell was again a co-founder and president, a role he held until 2011. Over that decade, the XL TechGroup platform generated approximately [$4.5 billion of public-market value through six IPOs](https://www.innventure.com/team/bill-haskell) on domestic U.S. and London Stock Exchange markets — a track record that established both his credibility and his practical literacy in IPO execution, capital markets timing, and the specific governance challenges of taking technology-platform companies public. The London Stock Exchange listing on which Haskell later served as chief executive — the precise dates of which are not fully disclosed in available materials — further extended that international capital-markets biography.

From 2019 to 2021, immediately before assuming the Innventure CEO role, Haskell was a partner at Bellview Associates, a boutique advisory firm focused on converting private companies into employee-owned enterprises. That interlude is more revealing than it might appear: employee-ownership conversion work requires deep competency in financial structuring, alignment architecture, and stakeholder negotiation — exactly the skill set required to manage the multi-stakeholder capital raises that now define Innventure's operational calendar. When Haskell became Innventure's CEO in 2021, he brought with him a profile defined less by sector expertise in cleantech, advanced materials, or data-center infrastructure, and more by institutional knowledge of how to build, fund, and govern early-stage technology companies at scale.

That profile is both the asset and the risk. As simultaneous CEO of the parent holding company while three operating businesses are each in their own critical commercialization phases, Haskell's most important function is systemic: hiring the right operating-company CEOs, ensuring capital reaches each subsidiary on time, and managing the investor narrative of a consolidated entity whose financials are still dominated by operating losses. Whether a generalist company-builder — however accomplished — can adequately steward the simultaneous commercial crises at Accelsius, AeroFlexx, and Refinity is the management question the market has not yet fully resolved.

## Mike Otworth: The Proof of Concept

If Haskell is Innventure's architect of process, [Mike Otworth](https://www.innventure.com/team/mike-otworth) is its primary reputational asset. His career began on Capitol Hill as a legislative aide and committee staff member — an origin that instilled a fluency in institutional relationships and coalition-building that would prove critical in negotiating technology licenses from major corporations. He joined XL TechGroup in 1996 and over the following four years founded multiple early-stage companies within the platform, developing the company-creation methodology that Innventure would later codify as the MATCH scoring framework and DownSelect process.

From 2008 to 2015, Otworth served as president and founding partner of Green Ocean Innovation, providing technology-sourcing and innovation-strategy services aligned with Lilly/Elanco Animal Health. The engagement is notable not merely as a biographical data point but as evidence that Otworth was refining the corporate-IP-to-startup pipeline model during the years between XL TechGroup and Innventure — stress-testing the methodology in a life-sciences context before applying it to materials science and engineering.
